newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Thumbnail sketches of nominees for top U.N. post.
newsitem.headline: Thumbnail sketches of nominees for top U.N. post.

text.p: Following are brief biographies of declared African candidates vying for U.N. secretary-general to succeed Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt, who has temporarily stepped aside in the race but not withdrawn completely. His term ends on December 31.

-- HAMID ALGABID of Niger, 55; serving an unprecedented second term as secretary-general of Organisation of Islamic Conference; prime minister of Niger from 1983 to 1988; previously served as ministers of commerce and finance; doctorate in law from University of Paris;

-- KOFI ANNAN of Ghana, 58; U.N. undersecretary-general for peacekeeping affairs; employed by the United Nations for more than 20 years, including head of budget, finance and personnel in New York and Geneva; degree in economics at Macalester College in Minnesota; postgraduate work at Insistute des Hautes Etudes Internationales in Geneva; masters from Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

-- AMARA ESSY of Ivory Coast, 51; foreign minister recently credited with helping to forge a peace pact in Sierra Leone's civil war; president of U.N. General Assembly, 1994-95; former ambassador to United Nations, Cuba and Argentina, Switzerland; represented his country at numerous international conferences in world and region; degree in public law; diploma from Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Geneva.

-- AHMEDOU OULD-ABDALLAH, of Mauritania, 55; executive secretary of the Global Coalition for Africa, a Washington-based forum for political and economic issues, headed by former World Bank president Robert McNamara, among others; special U.N. representative in Burundi 1993 to 1995; former minister of commerce and foreign affairs; former ambassador to the United States, the European Union, Belgium, Luxemberg and the Netherlands; degree from Univeristy of Grenobal and masters degree from University of Paris.

-- SALIM A. SALIM of Tanzania, 54; secretary-general of Organisation of African Unity; about to make his candidacy official, according to South African President Nelson Mandela; ambassador to Egypt at age 22; former U.N. ambassador, former foreign minister; vetoed by Reagan administration 15 times when he ran for the top U.N. post in 1981; earned masters degree from Columbia University while leading his country's delegation at United Nations.
